* Do not add `name` to `run` steps
* Use Docker layer caching with `cache-from` and `cache-to` (see Docker Cache Strategy below)
* Update image digests in Kustomization files after build
* Set `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress` based on trigger type (see Concurrency below)
* Always set `timeout-minutes` on jobs, taking 10 unless a run of that job has been measured to sit elsewhere - one measured in seconds takes 1, one measured past 10 takes 60, and one measured past 60 takes 300 - it caps the job rather than estimating it, so a figure taken to be safe rather than from a measurement is how long a hung job holds its runner and leaves its workflow run `in_progress` before anything cuts it, while a single shared default is what leaves any other figure readable as a measurement rather than as a guess
* Add `if: github.repository_owner == 'kaidotio'` to jobs that: (1) respond to events triggerable by non-owners (`pull_request`, `pull_request_target`, `issue_comment`, `issues`, `schedule`, `workflow_run`), or (2) depend on self-hosted runners, either by calling a reusable workflow that does (e.g., `scan` job calling `reusable_scan-image.yaml`) or by naming `self-hosted` in `runs-on:` themselves (`40_github-actions-runner-controller.yaml`), where a `workflow_call` workflow leaves the guard to its caller and carries none on its own jobs (`reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml`) - the public mirror `## Release Workflows` names carries no self-hosted runner, so such a job stays `Queued` there instead of failing. Not needed for `push: branches: main`, `release`, `workflow_dispatch` unless condition (2) applies. Release workflows (`20_*`) that build versioned artifacts carry it on no job so they still run on the public mirror, leaving the guard to the `runner` and `windows-runner` jobs alone where the local runner can take the build, while the `push:`-triggered `20_*` deploy workflows keep the guard (see Release Workflows)
* Where a condition alone decides whether the job does any work, put it on the job `if:` and never on a step, unless it reads a context the job level does not carry (`steps.*`, `matrix.*`) - the job-level one reports `skipped` without allocating a runner, while a job that starts and skips every step reports `success` and bills a full minute
* A `workflow_run` trigger with `types: [completed]` fires on every conclusion, so gate the job on `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion` as well, and where the workflow carries other triggers write it as `github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` - `github.event.workflow_run` is null under those events, so a bare conclusion test silently skips every one of them
* A workflow consuming another workflow's release assets carries a `workflow_run` trigger naming every workflow that produces them, and where that names more than one, a job ahead of the build that reads the release's asset list and gates the build on every consumed file being present - `release` fires while those workflows are still uploading their platform matrix, a `push`-only trigger never fires when a release lands at all, and `workflows:` is an OR, so each producer starts its own run and every one but the run the last producer started reaches the download mid-upload; `gh release download` exits 0 when only some of its `-p` patterns match, so the gap surfaces at the `install` that consumes the file rather than at the download, and the gate skips rather than fails because `claude-auto-fix-ci.yaml` reacts to every `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'failure'` (`00_ephemeral-container.yaml`)
* Pass the firing release's tag to every `gh release download` and `gh release view` in such a workflow as `"${RELEASE_TAG}"` with `RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.head_branch || '' }}` in the step's `env:` - an untagged call takes whichever release is latest when the run happens to start rather than the one the run reacted to, and `gh` reads an empty tag argument as that same latest-release fallback, so the workflow's other triggers keep their existing behaviour (`00_ephemeral-container.yaml`, `00_gemini-sandbox.yaml`, `00_tauri-releases.yaml`; `90_fillcsv.yaml` carries no `workflow_run` trigger, so the latest release is the right one there)
* Jobs depending on `runner` reusable workflow must use `!cancelled()` in their `if:` condition to handle partial failures (e.g., token server unavailable). See `.claude/reference/.github/workflows/creating-build-workflow.md` for exact patterns
* Workflows calling `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml` (or any workflow whose chain includes `reusable_issue-github-token.yaml`) must declare `id-token: write` in the top-level `permissions` block; GitHub Actions requires caller permissions to be a superset of the reusable workflow's permissions, otherwise the run fails with `startup_failure`
* Always derive a git branch name from `env.IMAGE` as `branch="${IMAGE//\//-}"`, never `branch="${IMAGE}"` (the substitution is a no-op when IMAGE has no slash). Git cannot create `refs/heads/foo` when `refs/heads/foo/bar` already exists; IMAGE values with slashes (e.g., `snapshot-controller/snapshot-diff-server`) cause a ref namespace collision that silently breaks the deploy step
* A `99_mirror-*` workflow spells the mirrored tag twice - `env.TAG` on the `mirror` job, and again inside the full `image:` handed to `reusable_scan-image.yaml` - so bump both in the same edit; `jobs.<job_id>.with` cannot read `env`, so no reference collapses them, and because the previous tag still resolves in GHCR a half-bump leaves the scan passing against the image that is no longer deployed and filing its CVE issues against that one, with nothing failing anywhere
* A `99_mirror-*` tag bump deploys nothing on its own - `mirror.sh` opens a separate digest PR and that is what ArgoCD syncs - so read the new version's release notes for configuration it removes, renames, or re-defaults and land the workload's own config change in the same commit as the tag; nothing between the edit and the cluster parses that configuration, since `50_kubectl-validation.yaml` stops at `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`, which checks the generated ConfigMap object and never the text it carries, so a removed option first surfaces as the workload crash-looping after the digest PR merges, while a changed default fails nowhere at all and only shows up as the workload quietly behaving differently - pin such a value explicitly rather than inheriting it
* Move the ref in a workload's `resources:` URL to the same release whenever a `99_mirror-*` `TAG` is bumped - `mirror.sh` runs only `kustomize edit set image`, so the digest moves while the CRDs and RBAC `kustomize build` fetches stay on the old ref, and those objects are valid enough that `50_kubectl-validation.yaml` passes them through `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`, leaving the new binary against a schema and a ServiceAccount that predate it until the controller reaches a field or a verb that version added (`cluster/manifests/vpa/base/kustomization.yaml` sat at `vpa-release-1.0` while its images were `1.2.1`)
* Shell code in `run` steps follows bash conventions from `.claude/rules/bash.md` (variable quoting, conditionals, pipefail patterns, regex flavor), and an `npm` invocation in one follows `.claude/rules/javascript.md`, whose flags are load-bearing where a package leans on a lifecycle hook
* Multi-line `run` steps: use `set -eo pipefail` (not `-u`, GitHub Actions environment variables are always defined; not `-E` either, since a `run` step installs no `ERR` trap for it to carry into functions and command substitutions)
* Cross-platform workflows with Windows runners: set `shell: bash` on steps using bash syntax (Windows defaults to PowerShell)
* Use `${{ runner.temp }}` for temporary files needed only during workflow execution; use `~` for persistent home directory references
* Keep a `paths` filter matching what should rerun the workflow - its own file, renamed along with it, plus every input the steps consume outside the primary content directory - and leave out both the shared `.github/` infrastructure every workflow would fire on and the manifest directories the job pushes digest updates back to, which would retrigger it in a loop, even though `sparse-checkout` needs them; GitHub validates no entry against the tree, so a stale or missing one silently never triggers
* Use `sparse-checkout` with the most specific path that covers the files actually used by the workflow (e.g., `app/.github/actions/` not `app/.github/`). When specifying individual file paths (not directories), add `sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false` — cone mode (the default) rejects file-level paths — and list the root configuration files no step names but the tools discover on their own (`.npmrc`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`), since a directory entry carries them along while a file list drops them and the tool silently falls back to its own default
* Before `actions/checkout`, add a conditional step `echo "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=${{ runner.temp }}/gitconfig" >> $GITHUB_ENV` that runs only on self-hosted local runners (`if: contains(needs.runner.outputs.runner, 'local')`), followed by `git config --global submodule.recurse false` as a separate step. This ensures `actions/checkout`'s internal `git config --global --add safe.directory` writes to the temp file instead of `~/.gitconfig` (self-hosted local runners need an explicit path; empty `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` causes `git config --global` to fail on GitHub-hosted runners). Write both steps without that condition where the job pins `runs-on: [self-hosted, local, Linux]` instead of resolving a runner through `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml` - such a job declares no `needs: runner`, so the guard resolves empty and never fires, leaving `actions/checkout` to write `safe.directory` into the runner's real `~/.gitconfig` (`claude.yaml`)
* Reference an action in this repository from a step as `uses: $/{path}`, never `uses: ./{path}` - `gh actions-lock` never follows a `./` action and refuses to write the lockfile while a `./` action uses another action (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)
* Rerun `gh actions-lock` after adding a workflow or changing any `uses:` so `.github/workflows/actions.lock` covers it - Dependabot refreshes lockfile entries only for workflows already in it (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)
* Before `uses: $/.github/actions/setup-docker` or `docker login`, add a conditional step `echo "DOCKER_CONFIG=${{ runner.temp }}/.docker" >> $GITHUB_ENV` that runs only on self-hosted local runners (`if: contains(needs.runner.outputs.runner, 'local')` in regular workflows, or `if: contains(inputs.runner, 'local')` / `if: contains(inputs.runs-on, 'local')` in reusable workflows). This prevents `docker login` from overwriting `~/.docker/config.json` with short-lived `ghs_` GitHub App installation tokens
* On jobs that run `uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` on self-hosted local runners, `mkdir -p ${{ runner.temp }}/claude-tmp` alongside the existing `claude-home` directory and set `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/claude-tmp` in the step's `env:` next to `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. The SDK's default `/tmp/claude-<uid>` directory is shared across jobs on persistent self-hosted local runners and can be left behind owned by a different uid by an earlier process, causing the action to fail with `Temp directory /tmp/claude-<uid> is owned by uid 0, expected <uid>. Refusing to use it`. Not needed on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners (`ubuntu-24.04`), where `/tmp` starts clean every run
* A guard written as `contains(needs.runner.outputs.runner, 'local')` needs the job to declare `needs: runner` — without it the context resolves to empty, so the positive form never fires and the negated form always does
* When using `bash .github/scripts/cleanup.sh` to free disk space for large builds, add `if: ${{ !contains(needs.runner.outputs.runner, 'local') }}` to skip it on self-hosted local runners. The system directories it removes are needed by the host system on persistent local runners but are safe to remove on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners — read `.github/scripts/cleanup.sh` for what it deletes
* Place `cleanup.sh` before any `actions/setup-*` step — it deletes `$AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY`, so a toolchain the job has already provisioned on the runner goes with it
* When a workflow uses `uv sync`/`uv run` with `actions/setup-python`, set `python-version` to match the project's `requires-python` lower bound in `pyproject.toml` and add `env: UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS: never` to the uv step. uv's `python-downloads` defaults to `automatic`, so a version mismatch silently downloads a managed interpreter and uses it instead of the one `actions/setup-python` provisioned
* Do not put steps that write fixed workspace-relative state files under a `parallel:` block, since concurrent steps share one workspace

## Docker Cache Strategy

| Build Time | Strategy | cache-to |
|------------|----------|----------|
| Normal (<60 min) | Local only | `type=local,mode=max,dest=...` |
| Long (>60 min) | Local + Registry | `type=local,... --cache-to type=registry,ref=$GHCR_IMAGE:cache,mode=max` |

Local cache is stored in a per-image directory (`docker-build/{IMAGE}`) to prevent cache collisions between parallel builds on shared runners.

Registry cache uses `:cache` tag (not `:main`) to avoid overwriting the production image.
Add registry cache when:
- Build exceeds 60 minutes (GitHub Actions cache may be evicted before next build)
- Dockerfile changes infrequently (Rust cross-compilation base images)

## Concurrency

Where the triggers a workflow declares match more than one row, take the row asking for `false` - a cancelled reactive or scheduled run is simply dropped, while a cancelled `push` run is superseded by the run that cancelled it.

| Trigger | `concurrency` | `cancel-in-progress` | Reason |
|---------|---------------|----------------------|--------|
| `push`, `pull_request`, `release` | Yes | `true` | Newer commit supersedes older |
| `pull_request_target` | Yes | `true` | Use `${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}` not `${{ github.ref }}`; under `pull_request_target`, `github.ref` always resolves to the base branch, causing all concurrent PRs to share one group and cancel each other |
| `workflow_dispatch` | Yes | `true` | User can re-trigger |
| `push` + `schedule` (mixed) | Yes | `true` | Push is primary trigger |
| `schedule` only | Yes | `false` | Current run should complete |
| `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` | Yes | `false` | Schedule is primary trigger; workflow_dispatch is manual re-trigger |
| `issue_comment`, `issues`, `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment` | No | - | Each event is independent; for `issue_comment`/`issues` `github.ref` is `refs/heads/main` causing unrelated events to share a concurrency group, and for `pull_request_review`/`pull_request_review_comment` each event should complete independently |
| `workflow_run` | Yes | `false` | Each reactive action must complete |

## Naming

| Prefix | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `00_` | Application Docker builds |
| `10_` | Event handlers (label, comment) |
| `20_` | Release/additional builds (armyknife, taurin, Cloudflare Workers) |
| `40_` | Tests |
| `50_` | Validation |
| `80_` | Metrics/sync |
| `90_` | Auto-generation (readme, crd, jsonnet), snapshots |
| `99_` | Mirroring |
| `reusable_` | Reusable workflow templates |
| (none) | AI integration (claude*.yaml) |

## Release Workflows

Release workflows (`20_*.yaml`) that build versioned artifacts:

1. Use sparse-checkout with `bin/` included for `bump.sh`
2. Extract version from tag: `VERSION=$(echo ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }} | sed 's/^v//')`
3. Call `bump.sh` before build: `bash ./bin/bump.sh "${VERSION}"`
4. Give a build job the local runner can take a `runner` job calling `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml` under the owner guard, as the deploy workflows do, and on the build job `needs: runner`, `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` and `runs-on: ${{ needs.runner.outputs.runner && fromJSON(needs.runner.outputs.runner) || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}` - in a platform matrix holding `windows-latest`, a `windows-runner` job beside it calling the same workflow with `labels: self-hosted,local,Windows` and `fallback-runner: windows-latest`, since `setup/hyperv-host/setup.ps1` registers the Windows runner apart from the Linux one and a Windows job sent to it while it is offline stays `Queued` instead of falling back, with `needs: [runner, windows-runner]` and `${{ matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-24.04' && (needs.runner.outputs.runner && fromJSON(needs.runner.outputs.runner) || 'ubuntu-24.04') || matrix.platform == 'windows-latest' && (needs.windows-runner.outputs.runner && fromJSON(needs.windows-runner.outputs.runner) || 'windows-latest') || matrix.platform }}` - so the public mirror, where the guard skips `runner`, still builds on the hosted runner, and with a workflow-level `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`, since a local runner's job otherwise inherits the developer's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which `bin/github-local-self-hosted-runner.sh` requires in its environment, and write its local-only steps under `contains(needs.runner.outputs.runner, 'local')`, under `contains(needs.windows-runner.outputs.runner, 'local')` where the step runs on Windows alone, or under `contains(matrix.platform == 'windows-latest' && needs.windows-runner.outputs.runner || matrix.platform != 'windows-latest' && needs.runner.outputs.runner, 'local')` where the step also runs on Windows - the second `matrix.platform` test keeps a Windows job whose `windows-runner` output is empty from reading the Linux one - adding `matrix.platform != 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' && ` where the matrix also holds an arm64 runner: the `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `DOCKER_CONFIG` steps, `cleanup.sh` and any `apt-get` step skipped (the Arch Linux local runners have no `apt-get`, so the host must already carry those packages), and `RUSTUP_HOME` alone pointed under `${{ runner.temp }}` before `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, which runs `rustup default` in the runner user's home, the host's own on a local runner - `CARGO_HOME` stays put, since the host's rustup then refuses `rustup toolchain add` beside a `rust-toolchain.toml` with `rustup is not installed at '<CARGO_HOME>'` - with the `~/.cargo/registry` cache step skipped, since restoring it would overwrite the host's own registry. Point `GRADLE_USER_HOME` under `${{ runner.temp }}` as well, since Gradle's user home otherwise defaults to `~/.gradle` (https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/directory_layout.html), with `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` given `cache-disabled` there, and `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT` ahead of `android-actions/setup-android`, which otherwise installs into `~/.android/sdk` (`20_plugin.yaml`, `20_taurim.yaml`). Skip on the Windows runner any toolchain install the `windows-latest` job runs, since `setup/hyperv-host/setup.ps1` provisions it on the host instead (the CUDA installer in `20_taurin.yaml`). Keep the direct-runner pattern (`runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`, or a platform matrix for cross-OS artifacts) for a job running on an arm64 runner, which no local runner is. Release workflows must run on the public mirror (`hippocampus-dev/hippocampus`), which has no self-hosted runners: release assets are published to the firing repository's release and pulled by unauthenticated clients from the public mirror (e.g., `remotty`'s `Dockerfile` and the `github-actions-runner-controller` runner image `ADD https://github.com/hippocampus-dev/hippocampus/releases/latest/download/...`, and the taurin and taurim updater endpoints `80_sync-public-repository.yaml` rewrites). An owner guard on the build job itself would skip it entirely there, leaving the public release without those binaries, and the `administration-reader` token `check` lists runners with is issued under a release's `refs/tags/v*` only because `cluster/manifests/hippocampus-dev-github-token-server/overlays/dev/github-token-server/authorization_policy.yaml` names that ref, so without it every release falls back to the hosted runner.
Use `bash` prefix because `bump.sh` lacks execute permission in the repository.

`bump.sh` handles sparse-checkout gracefully - uses `find` which ignores missing directories, and `if [ -f ... ]` checks for specific files.

Build a release with more than one target in a platform matrix running one job per target and upload each artifact with `gh release upload`, not with `goreleaser` - running the targets as parallel jobs and merging them into one release (`--split`, `goreleaser continue --merge`) requires GoReleaser Pro (https://goreleaser.com/customization/partial/), so open-source `goreleaser release` builds every target on the one runner it runs on, which also leaves no way to build natively per OS (such as Rust's MSVC toolchain on `windows-latest`).

Build a Rust release for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` with `cross build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, which takes the image `Cross.toml` names, rather than `cargo build` - `.cargo/config.toml` turns `crt-static` off for that target, so the binary requires whichever glibc symbol versions the building machine offers, and the image built from `cross/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.Dockerfile` pins them to glibc 2.17 wherever the job runs (`20_insight.yaml`, `20_confidant.yaml`, `20_teleput.yaml`).

## PR Trigger

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review]
```

Exclude drafts: `github.event.pull_request.draft == false && github.event.pull_request.state == 'open'`

## Runner Selection

| Condition | Runner |
|-----------|--------|
| Cluster internal access | `[self-hosted, github-actions-runner-controller, standard]` |
| Cluster internal access needing `docker build` | `[self-hosted, github-actions-runner-controller, userns]` |
| Cluster internal access needing a Docker daemon | `[self-hosted, github-actions-runner-controller, privileged]` |
| Local host assets only (`/home/kai/bin/hacklaudex`, `~/.config/claudex`, local `kubectl`, or token-issuing / runner-check reusable jobs) | `[self-hosted, local, Linux]` |
| Non-`pull_request` workflows that can run on the local runner (`00_*`, `push`-triggered `20_*`, `99_mirror-*`, and non-OIDC `10_*`, `80_*`, non-snapshot `90_*`) (prefer local, fall back to hosted) | `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml` with `labels: self-hosted,local,Linux`, `fallback-runner: ubuntu-24.04` (spelled as `bin/github-local-self-hosted-runner.sh` registers it, since its `check` job compares label names case-sensitively and otherwise always falls back) |
| Release workflows `20_*` that build versioned artifacts, for a job the local runner can take (must run on the public mirror) | `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml` as for deploy workflows, plus a second call with `labels: self-hosted,local,Windows` and `fallback-runner: windows-latest` for a Windows platform, with no owner guard on the build job (see Release Workflows) |
| Release workflows `20_*` that build versioned artifacts, for a job the local runner cannot take (must run on the public mirror) | `ubuntu-24.04`, or a platform matrix for cross-OS artifacts (no owner guard, no dynamic-runner) |
| Pull request workflows (`40_*`, `50_kubectl-validation.yaml`, `claude-code-review.yaml`, PR-triggered `10_*`), hosted OIDC callers (`token-request-server-public.kaidotio.dev` / `cortex-api-public.kaidotio.dev`), and intentionally hosted snapshots (`90_*snapshot*.yaml`) | `ubuntu-24.04` (pass `runs-on: '["ubuntu-24.04"]'` explicitly when calling `reusable_snapshot.yaml` or `reusable_scheduled-snapshot.yaml` rather than relying on their default) |

`standard`, `userns` and `privileged` name the `runnerContainerSpec.isolation` each pool carries - `standard` names the pool carrying none - rather than decorating it, since the controller registers `self-hosted` and `github-actions-runner-controller` for every workload it creates and a `runs-on` naming only those two therefore matches all of them.
No row holds a Kubernetes API token, since every pool runs as the `runner` service account with `automountServiceAccountToken: false` - a job that needs the API server, as `50_kubectl-validation.yaml` does, creates its own kind cluster on `ubuntu-24.04` instead, so pull request code never runs next to credentials for the real cluster.

A job taking the `privileged` row finds the daemon already running, since the pool starts it from the job started hook (`cluster/applications/privileged-runner/README.md`), so it neither starts one itself nor gives up `container:` and `services:` - the `userns` row reaches a `docker build` through the rootless podman that isolation enables (`cluster/applications/github-actions-runner-controller/README.md`'s `### Rootless Runner`) but leaves no daemon for the runner to create service containers through, so send a job needing `container:` or `services:` to the `privileged` row.
Only the `userns` and `privileged` rows answer a `docker` command, since the rendered Dockerfile installs the podman-docker shim for `runnerContainerSpec.isolation: userns` alone and the `privileged` image carries the real client besides (`cluster/applications/privileged-runner/Dockerfile`), so a job sending one to the `standard` row fails on `docker: command not found`.

Keep `pull_request` workflows on `ubuntu-24.04` rather than `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml`, since `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml` runs under `environment: deployment` (blocked on `refs/pull/N/merge`; see `## Secrets`) and `cluster/manifests/hippocampus-dev-github-token-server/overlays/dev/github-token-server/authorization_policy.yaml` limits token issuance to `refs/heads/main` and `refs/tags/v*`.
Use `reusable_dynamic-runner.yaml` for every other workflow that has no local-only or cluster-only dependency and is not intentionally pinned to GitHub-hosted runners (`90_*snapshot*.yaml` and jobs calling `token-request-server-public.kaidotio.dev` / `cortex-api-public.kaidotio.dev` via OIDC), so jobs run locally when the host is up and fall back to hosted runners when offline.
Pin `[self-hosted, local, Linux]` only where a job cannot fall back because it relies on files, credentials or tools provisioned solely on the local host.
For `anthropics/claude-code-action` workflows, choose `/home/kai/bin/hacklaudex` on `[self-hosted, local, Linux]` when the job needs local tools or credentials (`kubectl`, local MCP servers, local auth) or can wait in the queue while the local host is offline without VM isolation (`claude.yaml`, `10_triage-loganomaly.yaml`, `claude-auto-fix-ci.yaml`), and choose `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` with `CLAUDE.ci.md` on `ubuntu-24.04` when it needs disposable-VM isolation (such as `pull_request` triggers) or availability while the local host is off (`claude-code-review.yaml`).

When installing binaries at runtime (e.g., `goreleaser`, `cross`), extract to `${{ runner.temp }}/bin` and append to `$GITHUB_PATH` (`echo "${{ runner.temp }}/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"`) rather than `/usr/local/bin`.
`github-actions-runner-controller` runners run as uid 60000 and reach a root-owned `/usr/local/bin` only through `sudo`, and self-hosted local runners would retain system-wide binaries across runs; `${{ runner.temp }}` is writable on all runner types and auto-cleans per job.

## Path Exclusions

Exclude non-source files from build triggers:

```yaml
paths:
  - "!**/*.md"
  - "!**/manifests/**"
  - "!**/skaffold/**"
```

## Secrets

Secrets are managed via `bin/repository-settings.sh`.
Add new secrets to the appropriate array.

| Scope | Array | `environment` required |
|-------|-------|------------------------|
| All workflows | `repository_secrets` | No |
| Protected deployments | `environment_secrets` | `deployment` |

Jobs that access `environment_secrets` (e.g., `GPG_PASSPHRASE`) must set `environment: deployment`.
This includes external service deployments (Cloudflare, Tauri signing) and token-issuing jobs and the jobs that decrypt their GPG-encrypted tokens.

When the job must access `environment_secrets` and is triggered by a Dependabot PR (or any external contributor), use `pull_request_target` instead of `pull_request`.
GitHub's environment protection rules block the `refs/pull/N/merge` context produced by `pull_request` events; `pull_request_target` runs in the base branch context, satisfying protection rules.
Do not check out or execute any PR code in these workflows.

Steps that run raw `gh` CLI commands (e.g., `gh pr view`, `gh pr comment`) without `actions/checkout` must set `GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}` in the step's `env:` block.
`gh` normally infers the target repository from the local git remote; without a checkout there is no git repository, causing `gh` to fail with `fatal: not a git repository`.

## Reference

If creating a new build workflow:
